SupporterRules.notice: Manages the rules and data specific to Supporter users within the community.

INVITER_PERCENTAGE.notice: Commission percentage paid to the inviter when an invited supporter burns tokens.

MAX_COMMITMENTS.notice: The maximum number of commitments for supporters.

addSupporter.notice: Allows a new user to register as a Supporter.
addSupporter.details: Registers the sender as a Supporter, assigning them a unique ID and updating CommunityRules. Requires name and profile photo length to be within limits.

params.description: Brief description of the the supporter (max 200 characters).
params.name: The name of the supporter (max 100 characters).
params.profilePhoto: The profile photo URL/hash of the supporter (max 150 characters).

calculatorItemCertificates.notice: The relationship between address and burned tokens per calculator item.

declareReductionCommitment.notice: Allows a supporter to declare a reduction commitment for a specific calculator item.
declareReductionCommitment.details: Records the calculator item ID as a commitment for the calling supporter. Requires the calculator item to exist and the sender to be a registered supporter.

params.calculatorItemId: The ID of the CalculatorItem for which the commitment is being declared.

declaredReduction.notice: The relationship between an address and a mapping of items ids and booleans if declared commitment or not.

getReductionCommitments.notice: Retrieves the list of reduction commitment item IDs for a specific address.

params.addr: The address of the supporter.

returns._0: uint256[] An array of calculator item IDs representing the commitments.

getSupporter.notice: Returns the detailed information of a supporter.
getSupporter.details: Retrieves the full Supporter struct data for a specific address.

params.addr: The address of the supporter.

returns._0: Supporter The `Supporter` struct containing their data.

offset.notice: Allows a supporter to burn tokens to compensate for a specific item's degradation, with a message to the community. Before calling this function, supporters must approve the SupporterRules contract to burn the required amount oftokens.
offset.details: This function calls the token transfer function to pay comissions and burnFrom to trade tokens for the compensation certificate. If a valid calculatorItemId is provided, records the burned amount as a certificate for that item.

params.amount: Tokens to be burned (minimum 1 token in wei, i.e., 1e18).
params.calculatorItemId: The ID of the CalculatorItem, or 0 if not applicable.
params.minAmountToBurn: Slippage protection: the minimum amount the user expects to burn after commission.

offsets.notice: The relationship between offset id and its data.

offsetsCount.notice: Total number of offsets made across all supporters.

reductionCommitments.notice: The relationship between address and reduction commitment statements (stored as calculator item IDs).

supportersAddress.notice: The relationship between ID and supporter address.

updateProfilePhoto.notice: Allows a supporter to update their profile photo.
updateProfilePhoto.details: Updates the 'profilePhoto' field for the calling supporter. Only accessible by registered supporters, and enforces a max character limit.

params.newPhoto: User's new profile photo URL/hash (max 150 characters).

constructor.details: Initializes the SupporterRules contract with addresses of crucial external contracts.

params.researcherRulesAddress: Address of the ResearcherRules contract, used for CalculatorItem data.

ActivistRules.notice: This contract defines and manages the rules and data specific to "Activist" users within the system. Activists are responsible for inviting new Regenerators and Inspectors, and they earn rewards based on the approval of their invited users.

MAX_USER_COUNT.notice: Maximum users count allowed for this UserType.

MINIMUM_INSPECTIONS_TO_WON_POOL_LEVELS.notice: Minimum inspections an inviter must complete to add activist level.

activistPool.notice: The address of the `ActivistPool` contract, responsible for managing and distributing token rewards to activists.

activistsAddress.notice: A public mapping from a unique activist ID to their corresponding wallet address. Facilitates lookup of an activist's address by their ID.

addActivist.notice: Users must meet specific criteria (previously invitation, system proportionality) to successfully register as an activist. Requirements: - The caller (`msg.sender`) must not already be a registered user. - The `name` and `proofPhoto` strings must not exceed 100 characters in byte length. - The total number of `ACTIVIST` users in the system must not exceed 16,000.
addActivist.details: Allows a user to attempt to register as an activist. Creates a new `Activist` profile for the caller if all requirements are met.

params.name: The chosen name for the activist.
params.proofPhoto: A hash or identifier for the activist's identity verification photo.

addInspectorLevel.notice: This function should be called by the InspectionRules contract after an Inspector completes their required inspections.
addInspectorLevel.details: External function for authorized callers to add a pool level to an activist when an invited Inspector reaches the minimum inspection threshold.

params.inspectorAddress: The wallet address of the invited Inspector.
params.inspectorTotalInspections: The total number of inspections completed by the Inspector.

addRegeneratorLevel.notice: This function should be called by the InspectionRules contract. after a Regenerator completes their required inspections.
addRegeneratorLevel.details: External function for authorized callers to add a pool level to an activist when an invited Regenerator reaches the minimum inspection threshold.

params.regeneratorAddress: The wallet address of the invited Regenerator.
params.regeneratorTotalInspections: The total number of inspections completed by the Regenerator.

approvedInvites.notice: The total count of all invitations that have been successfully approved across the entire system.

canInvite.notice: Checks if a user is eligible to send an invitation.
canInvite.details: Eligibility rules: 1. If the total number of users in the system is less than or equal to `INITIAL_USER_COUNT_THRESHOLD`, any user can invite (returns true). 2. Otherwise, a user can invite if their `userLevels` are greater than or equal to the average levels per user plus one (`avg = (totalLevels / totalUsers) + 1`).

params.totalLevels: The total levels accumulated by all users of a specific type in the system.
params.totalUsers: The total number of users of a specific type registered in the system.
params.userLevels: The total levels of the specific user wishing to invite.

returns._0: bool True if the user can invite, false otherwise.

canSendInvite.notice: Returns `true` if the activist can send an invite, `false` otherwise.
canSendInvite.details: Checks if a specific activist address is eligible to send new invitations.

params.addr: The address of the activist to check.

returns._0: bool `true` if the activist is eligible to send an invite, `false` otherwise.

communityRules.notice: The address of the `CommunityRules` contract, used to interact with community-wide rules, user types, and invitation data.

getActivist.notice: Provides the full profile of an activist.
getActivist.details: Returns the detailed `Activist` data for a given address.

params.addr: The address of the activist to retrieve.

returns._0: Activist The `Activist` struct containing the user's data.

isAllowedCaller.notice: Checks if a given address is currently in the list of allowed callers.

returns._0: bool True if the address is an allowed caller, false otherwise.

poolCurrentEra.notice: This function provides the current era from the perspective of the reward pool.
poolCurrentEra.details: Returns the current era as determined by the `ActivistPool` contract.

returns._0: uint256 The current era of the `ActivistPool`.

removePoolLevels.notice: Can only be called by the ValidationRules contract.
removePoolLevels.details: Allows an authorized caller to remove levels from an activist's pool. This function updates the activist's local level if user is not being denied  and notifies the `ActivistPool` contract to remove the pool level.

params.addr: The wallet address of the activist from whom levels are to be removed.

totalActiveLevels.notice: The sum of all active levels from non-denied activists. Used for governance calculations.

withdraw.notice: Activists can claim tokens for the services provided. The distribution is proportional to the amount of approved users in the current era. Requirements: - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be a registered `ACTIVIST`. - The activist must have approvedUsers in their current era. - The activist's current era (`activist.pool.currentEra`) will be incremented upon successful withdrawal attempt.
withdraw.details: Allows an activist to initiate a withdrawal of Regeneration Credits based on their approved invited users and current era.

CommunityRules.notice: This contract serves as the central registry for user management within the community. It manages user types, registration processes, invitation mechanisms, and a delation system for reporting unwanted behavior.

SUPPORTER_INVITATION_DELAY_BLOCKS.notice: The number of blocks an invitation is delayed for Supporters.

VOTER_INVITATION_DELAY_BLOCKS.notice: The number of blocks an invitation is delayed for voter-type users.

addDelation.notice: Allows registered users (excluding Supporters) to report other users or resources that may require invalidation. Limited to one delation per target. Examples of unwanted behavior: - A user voting to invalidate a valid resource - User without valid proofPhoto - Inspections without valid proofPhoto - Inspections without valid justification report - Resources without valid justifications report - Inactive users
addDelation.details: Adds a new delation to the system. Enforces character limits for title and testimony, and requires both reporter and reported user to be registered.

params.addr: The address of the user being reported.
params.title: Title of the delation (Max 100 characters).

addInvitation.notice: Attempts to add an invitation for a new user.

params.invited: The address of the user who received the invitation.
params.inviter: The address of the user who issued the invitation.
params.userType: The `UserType` the `invited` user is intended to register as.

addInviterPenalty.notice: This functions adds a penalty to users when a invited user gets denied.
addInviterPenalty.details: This function is intended to be called by an allowed caller (`ValidationRules`). It decrements the count of penalties for the inviter.

params.inviter: The address of the inviter receiving the penalty.

addUser.notice: Adds a new user to the system with a specified user type.
addUser.details: This function can only be called by an allowed caller (e.g., specific *Rules contracts for each user type). It enforces rules for single registration per address, valid user types, proportionality limits, and valid invitations if required.

params.addr: The address of the user to be registered.

constructor.notice: Initializes the CommunityRules contract by setting up initial proportionality and invitation rules for various user types.
constructor.details: Sets predefined `UserTypeSetting` for Regenerators, Inspectors, Activists, Researchers, Developers, and Contributors.

params.activistProportionality: Defines the proportionality ratio for Activist registration.
params.contributorProportionality: Defines the proportionality ratio for Contributor registration.
params.developerProportionality: Defines the proportionality ratio for Developer registration.
params.inspectorProportionality: Defines the proportionality ratio for Inspector registration.
params.researcherProportionality: Defines the proportionality ratio for Researcher registration.

delationsById.notice: A mapping from a delation id to the `Delation` struct.

delationsCount.notice: Total count of delations received across all users.

getInvitation.notice: Get the invitation of a user.

params.addr: User address.

returns._0: the Invitation data struct.

getUser.notice: Returns the `UserType` of a given address.

params.addr: The address to query.

returns._0: UserType The `UserType` enum value associated with the address.

getUserDelations.notice: Gets the unique IDs of all delations filed against a user.
getUserDelations.details: This function returns an array of IDs. The full data for each delation can then be fetched individually from the public `delationsById` mapping.

params._user: The address of the user whose delation IDs are to be retrieved.

returns._0: An array of `uint64` delation IDs.

getUserTypeSettings.notice: Returns the `UserTypeSetting` configuration for a specific `UserType`.

returns._0: UserTypeSetting The `UserTypeSetting` struct containing configuration data.

invitations.notice: A mapping from an invited user's address to their `Invitation` details.

inviterPenalties.notice: Tracks the number of times an inviter has had their invitees denied.

isAllowedCaller.notice: Checks if a given address is currently in the list of allowed callers.

returns._0: bool True if the address is an allowed caller, false otherwise.

isDenied.notice: Function to check if an userAddress is denied.

returns._0: bool True if userAddress is denied.

isVoter.notice: Checks if a given address belongs to a user type that is considered a voter.

params.addr: The address of the user to check.

returns._0: bool True if the user is a voter, false otherwise.

lastDelationBlock.notice: Tracks the block number of each user's last submitted delation.

setToDenied.details: This function is intended to be called by an allowed caller (`ValidationRules`). It decrements the count of the user's previous type and sets their `UserType` to `DENIED`. Prevents re-denying an already denied user.

params.userAddress: The address of the user to be denied.

userTypeIs.notice: Function to check if an userAddress type is equal passed userType.
userTypeIs.details: This function also checks if a user is denied, returning false if denied.

returns._0: bool True if userAddress is equal userType.

userTypeSettings.notice: A mapping storing specific settings for each `UserType`, including proportionality rules, invitation requirements, and voter status.

userTypesCount.notice: A mapping to track the count of active users for each `UserType`.

userTypesTotalCount.notice: A mapping to track the total count of registered users for each `UserType`, including both active and `DENIED` users. This count serves as a global counter for new user IDs.

usersCount.notice: The global total count of all active (non-`UNDEFINED`) users in the system..

voteOnDelation.notice: Allows users to vote (true/false) on an existing delation.
voteOnDelation.details: This creates a social validation layer. Voters cannot be the informer or the reported user.

params._delationId: The ID of the delation to vote on.
params._supportsDelation: True for a "thumbs up" (agrees), false for "thumbs down" (disagrees).

votersCount.notice: Returns the total count of users currently classified as voters.
votersCount.details: Sums the active counts of Activist, Contributor, Developer, and Researcher user types.

returns._0: uint256 The total number of voters.

hasWaitedRequiredTime.details: Calculates if a user is eligible to publish a delation. Eligibility based on the `lastDelationBlock` and `BLOCKS_BETWEEN_DELATIONS`.

params.addr: The address to check.

returns._0: `true` if the user can publish, `false` otherwise.

newAllowedCaller.details: Allows the contract owner to add a new address to the list of allowed callers. If ownership is renounced, this function can no longer be performed.

params.allowed: The address to add to the allowed callers list.

owner.details: Returns the address of the current owner.

renounceOwnership.details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. _delationIdsForUser.notice: Index of delation IDs for each reported user.

ContributorRules.notice: This contract defines and manages the rules and data specific to "Contributor" users within the system. Contributors perform generic contributions to the project and are subject to validation and penalty mechanisms.

MAX_USER_COUNT.notice: Maximum users count allowed for this UserType.

addContribution.notice: Contributions can only be published if certain time conditions and user type requirements are met. Requirements: - The `description` string must not exceed 300 characters in byte length. - The `report` hash/identifier string must not exceed 150 characters in byte length. - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be a registered `CONTRIBUTOR`. - The current block number must be greater than `securityBlocksToValidation` blocks away from the end of the current era (not within the security window). - The contributor must be eligible to publish based on `timeBetweenWorks` (checked via `canPublishContribution`).
addContribution.details: Allows a contributor to attempt to publish a new contribution report.

params.description: A title or brief description of the contribution.
params.report: A hash or identifier (e.g., IPFS CID) of the detailed report file.

addContributionValidation.notice: Only authorized validators can initiate this process after meeting specific requirements. Requirements: - The `justification` string must not exceed 300 characters in byte length. - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be eligible to vote (checked via `voteRules.canVote`). - The caller must have waited the required `timeBetweenVotes` (checked via `validationRules.waitedTimeBetweenVotes`). - The target `contribution` must exist and be currently valid, and its era must be the current era or a past one.
addContributionValidation.details: Allows a validator to cast a vote to invalidate a specific contribution. This process increments the validation count for the contribution and may trigger its invalidation.

params.id: The unique ID of the contribution to be validated/invalidated.
params.justification: A string explaining why the contribution is being invalidated.

addContributor.notice: Users must meet specific criteria (previous invitation, system vacancies) to successfully register as a contributor. Requirements: - The caller (`msg.sender`) must not already be a registered contributor. - The `name` string must not exceed 50 characters in byte length. - The `proofPhoto` string must not exceed 150 characters in byte length. - The total number of `CONTRIBUTOR` users in the system must not exceed 16,000.
addContributor.details: Allows a user to attempt to register as a contributor. Creates a new `Contributor` profile for the caller if all requirements are met.

params.name: The chosen name for the contributor.
params.proofPhoto: A hash or identifier for the contributor's identity verification photo.

canInvite.notice: Checks if a user is eligible to send an invitation.
canInvite.details: Eligibility rules: 1. If the total number of users in the system is less than or equal to `INITIAL_USER_COUNT_THRESHOLD`, any user can invite (returns true). 2. Otherwise, a user can invite if their `userLevels` are greater than or equal to the average levels per user plus one (`avg = (totalLevels / totalUsers) + 1`).

params.totalLevels: The total levels accumulated by all users of a specific type in the system.
params.totalUsers: The total number of users of a specific type registered in the system.
params.userLevels: The total levels of the specific user wishing to invite.

returns._0: bool True if the user can invite, false otherwise.

canPublishContribution.notice: This function determines if a contributor has waited the required time since their last publication.
canPublishContribution.details: Checks if a user can publish a new contribution based on `timeBetweenWorks`.

params.addr: The address of the contributor to check.

returns._0: bool `true` if the contributor can publish a contribution, `false` otherwise.

canSendInvite.notice: Returns `true` if the contributor can send an invite, `false` otherwise.
canSendInvite.details: Checks if a specific contributor address is eligible to send new invitations.

params.addr: The address of the contributor to check.

returns._0: bool `true` if the contributor is eligible to send an invite, `false` otherwise.

communityRules.notice: The interface of the `CommunityRules` contract, used to interact with community-wide rules, user types, and invitation data.

contributionPenalized.notice: Tracks contribution IDs that have already been invalidated.

contributions.notice: A mapping from a unique contribution ID to its detailed `Contribution` data structure. Stores all submitted contributions.

contributionsCount.notice: The total count of contributions that are currently considered valid (not invalidated).

contributionsIds.notice: A mapping from a contributor's wallet address to an array of IDs of contributions they have made.

contributionsTotalCount.notice: The total count of all contributions ever submitted, including invalidated ones. This acts as a global unique ID counter for new contributions.

contributorPool.notice: The interface of the `ContributorPool` contract, responsible for managing and distributing token rewards to contributors.

contributorsAddress.notice: A mapping from a unique contributor ID to their corresponding wallet address. Facilitates lookup of a contributor's address by their ID.

getContribution.notice: Provides the full details of a specific contribution.
getContribution.details: Returns the detailed `Contribution` data for a given contribution ID.

params.id: The unique ID of the contribution to retrieve.

returns._0: Contribution The `Contribution` struct containing the contribution's data.

getContributionsIds.notice: Provides a list of all contributions made by a given user.
getContributionsIds.details: Returns an array of IDs of the contributions made by a specific address.

params.addr: The address of the contributor whose contributions are to be retrieved.

returns._0: uint256[] An array of contribution IDs.

getContributor.notice: Provides the full profile of a contributor.
getContributor.details: Returns the detailed `Contributor` data for a given address.

params.addr: The address of the contributor to retrieve.

returns.contributor: The `Contributor` struct containing the user's data.

isAllowedCaller.notice: Checks if a given address is currently in the list of allowed callers.

returns._0: bool True if the address is an allowed caller, false otherwise.

maxPenalties.notice: The maximum number of penalties a contributor can accumulate before being denied.

nextEraIn.notice: Provides a countdown to the next era for contribution planning.
nextEraIn.details: Calculates the number of blocks remaining until the start of the next era, according to the `ContributorPool` contract's era definition.

returns._0: uint256 The amount of blocks remaining until the next era begins.

penalties.notice: A mapping from a contributor's wallet address to an array of `Penalty` structs they have received.

poolCurrentEra.notice: This function provides the current era from the perspective of the reward pool.
poolCurrentEra.details: Returns the current era as determined by the `ContributorPool` contract.

returns._0: uint256 The current era of the `ContributorPool`.

removePoolLevels.notice: Can only be called by ValidationRules address.
removePoolLevels.details: Allows an authorized caller to remove levels from a contributor's pool. This function updates the contributor's local level if user is not being denied and notifies the `ContributorPool` contract to remove the pool level.

params.addr: The wallet address of the contributor from whom levels are to be removed.

securityBlocksToValidation.notice: The number of blocks before the end of an era during which no new contributions can be published. This period allows validators sufficient time to analyze and vote on contributions before the era concludes.

timeBetweenWorks.notice: The minimum number of blocks that must elapse between contribution publications. This prevents spamming or rapid consecutive contributions.

totalActiveLevels.notice: The sum of all active levels from valid contributions by non-denied contributors.

totalPenalties.notice: Provides the current penalty count for a specific contributor.
totalPenalties.details: Returns the total number of penalties an address has accumulated.

params.addr: The contributor's wallet address.

returns._0: uint256 The total number of penalties for the given address.

validationRules.notice: The interface of the `ValidationRules` contract, which defines the rules and processes for validating or invalidating contributions.

voteRules.notice: The interface of the `VoteRules` contract, which defines rules for user voting eligibility, particularly for contribution validation.

withdraw.notice: Contributors can claim tokens for their contribution service. Requirements: - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be a registered `CONTRIBUTOR`. - The contributor must be eligible for withdrawal in their current era (checked via `contributorPool.canWithdraw`). - The contributor's current era (`contributor.pool.currentEra`) will be incremented upon successful withdrawal attempt.
withdraw.details: Allows a contributor to initiate a withdrawal of Regeneration Credits based on their published contributions and current era.

acceptInspection.notice: Inspectors must only accept inspections they are capable of performing, being aware of the safety risks and responsibilities. By accepting an inspection, inspectors agree that the they are responsible for their own safety at the data collection. It is recommended to use long sleeves clothes, hats, boots that can prevent bites from animals, gloves to protect from spines and any other useful safety equipment, such as machetes or pepper spray. Accepting an inspection counts as a 'give-up' until realized. Inspectors can only accept one open inspection at a time and cannot inspect the same regenerator twice. They must also adhere to specific delays and security windows. Requirements: - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be a registered `INSPECTOR`. - The inspector must have less than `MAX_GIVEUPS` (from InspectorRules). - The `inspectionId` must correspond to an existing inspection. - The inspector must not already have an inspection `ACCEPTED` that is not yet `INSPECTED` or `INVALIDATED` or `EXPIRED`. - The inspector must not have previously inspected this specific regenerator. - The inspection's status must be `OPEN` or `EXPIRED`. - The `acceptInspectionDelayBlocks` must have passed since the inspection was created. - The system must not be within the `securityBlocksToValidation` window before an era ends. - The inspector must adhere to `inspectorRules.canAcceptInspection` (delay from last realized inspection). - The `inspection.regenerator` must be a valid `REGENERATOR`.

Requirements: - The `justification` string must not exceed `MAX_VALIDATION_JUSTIFICATION_LENGTH` (300) characters. - The caller (`msg.sender`) must be a registered `voter` (`voteRules.canVote`). - The caller must have waited the required `timeBetweenVotes` (from `validationRules.waitedTimeBetweenVotes`). - The `inspectionId` must correspond to an existing and currently valid inspection. - The inspection must have been realized (`INSPECTED` status). - The current `poolCurrentEra() must be less than or equal to the `inspection's `inspectedAtEra` .

How many trees, palm trees and other plants over 1m high and 3cm in diameter there is in the regenerating area? Justify your answer in the report. How many different species of those plants/trees were found? Each different species is equivalent to one unity and only trees and plants managed or planted by the regenerator should be counted. Justify your answer in the report. Max result of 200.000 trees and 300 biodiversity. Zero score means invalid inspection. NOTE: If the inspector finds something suspicous about the inspected regenerator, such as invalid area, suspicious of fake account, or if the Regenerator is not findable, inspectors are encourage to realize passing 0 as values with his justification at the report to avoid being penalized.

params.thesis: A short description or thesis statement (Max characters).
params.title: The title of the research paper (max 100 characters).

If the validation count meets the threshold (`votesToInvalidate`), the research is marked as invalid.

RegenerationCreditImpact.notice: This contract is responsible for calculating the system impact and also the impact per token. The community impact backs the Regeneration Credit, it is the foundation of the System.

CARBON_PER_TREE.notice: [g] This constant estimates an average carbon sequestration of 100000g (or 100kg) per tree, palm tree and other plants with over 3cm in diameter and 1 meter high recorded by inspectors. In practice, it is not so simple to make this relationship, as the actual amount of carbon sequestered will vary from species to species, from biome to biome, from soil to soil, from management to management and from each geolocation. However, we need to standardize this value to simplify and allow the decentralized certification system to occur. This result was obtained by estimating that, on average, each tree/plant sequesters 10 kg of carbon per year, living an average of 10 years. With the result expressed in grams [g].

areaPerToken.notice: Calculates the area impact per Regeneration Credit. The effectiveSupply is the sum of currently circulating tokens (total supply minus locked) AND all tokens that have ever been burned (certified). This provides an impact metric based on all tokens that have contributed to or represent impact, whether currently in circulation or already consumed.

currentEpoch.notice: Epochs are 1-indexed. The calculation ensures that each epoch (including the first) comprises exactly `halving` eras, aligning with a conceptual 0-indexed era system for epoch grouping. For example, assuming halving = 12: Eras 1-12 (contract era numbers) -> Epoch 1 Eras 13-24 (contract era numbers) -> Epoch 2 And so on.
